claims.text: The initial material is as-cast HfMoTaTiZr.
Precipitates or secondary phases should be introduced into HfMoTaTiZr.
TiO and Al2O3 are proposed examples of the introduced phases.
Introducing TiO, Al2O3, or other secondary phases will reduce the density of HfMoTaTiZr.
Introducing the secondary phases will preserve the alloy's room-temperature mechanical performance.
Introducing the secondary phases will preserve the alloy's high-temperature mechanical performance.
The introduced precipitates or secondary phases will refine the grain structure.
Grain refinement and the introduced phases will improve the alloy's mechanical properties.
The modified alloy will maintain or improve yield strength.
The modified alloy will have improved fracture toughness.
As-cast HfMoTaTiZr has a density of 10.21 g cm−3.
As-cast HfMoTaTiZr has a room-temperature yield strength of 1600 MPa.
As-cast HfMoTaTiZr has an elevated-temperature yield strength of 855 MPa.
The proposed performance envelope extends from room temperature to 1600 °C.
Yield strength and fracture toughness are the specified mechanical response variables.
The exact density reduction and mechanical-property improvement are uncertain and require experimental verification.

contradictions.description: The hypothesis permits mechanical properties to be maintained without improvement, whereas the falsification rule rejects the hypothesis if mechanical properties do not improve. Thus an outcome with reduced density and unchanged strength would satisfy the stated hypothesis but fail its rejection rule.
